generic: Most separate observer lines name the attacker but not the exit direction (e.g. miss beginner 'attacks but misses!', prepare master[0], wait master[0], every weak/normal/heavy/critical/fumble separate observer); adding towards the {exitname} would let the attacker's room see where the attack went.

coupdegrace separate observer lines name {actee}, which the attacker's room cannot see by the separate sight rules; its remote lines also write {entrancename} without the exit ansi tag the rest of the file uses.
prepare together beginner[2]: actor faces the target 'nervously' while actee and observer read 'menacingly'; same action, mismatched tone.
heavy together master[3] actee 'From {actor}'s {stance} stance, {momentum}, they deliver...' reads awkwardly; stance and momentum are correctly the attacker's.
normal separate master[1] actor 'devastating accuracy' sits hot for a normal hit.
fumble together master[1]: actor blames a misstep while actee credits reading the telegraph; compatible but two causes.
Several separate actee lines never address the defender as 'you' (fumble beginner[0], expert[0], expert[2], expert[3], master[0]); they read from the defender's view, left as is.
heavy together beginner[0] and critical together expert[0] actee lines ('delivers a powerful blow!', 'delivers a PERFECT STRIKE!') do not say 'you'; implied, left as is.
Separate lines say 'shot' in places although generic covers any weapon; ranged by nature in this split, left as is.
shooting: critical separate: attacker-room observer lines carry no banner (that room cannot see the hit); the banner guard flags all nine, left for the owner to rule on.
fumble lines say arrow and bowstring, and miss and wait lines say trigger, though shooting also covers slings, crossbows and guns.
normal together expert[0] actee reads 'fires you decisively', missing 'at'.
critical together master[6] and beginner[1] actee lines never address the defender as you.
miss together master[2] actee says deflects while actor and room say evasion.
wait together beginner[0] actee and room have the attacker circling while the actor only aims.
weak separate beginner[1] and fumble separate beginner[2] attacker-room observers name a target that room cannot see.
heavy together master[2], [7] and [12] room lines dropped brutal precision, overwhelming and devastating to fit the target in 80 characters.
unarmed: normal/master[0]: room line calls the crisp counter a devastating counter and drops the body part; pairs, left as is.
critical/master[3]: room line says reads completely where the other roles say seizes the moment; pairs, left as is.
prepare/beginner[1]: attacker puts fists up bracing while the others say squares up; same act, left as is.
critical/expert[3] and critical/master[0]: room lines already name the target; no change.
